text:
frank-oncall: Heads-up — customer reported partial SSE chat output. The stream starts, we send first event, then client sees ~120 bytes and no more for ~25s, then the rest arrives as a big flush. Happening on hosted in us-east-1. Request IDs: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0a1b2c3e. They provided a curl repro and a proxy trace but we can't repro from our side yet. Pasting their curl below and attaching logs they sent.

maya-support: Thanks — can you paste exact timestamps and model/endpoint they hit? I'll ask them for a debug bundle (pcap/ngrep + curl with --no-buffer).

frank-oncall: Model: gpt-redwood-mini-v1, endpoint: https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat (SSE). Customer timestamps: 2025-11-04T14:02:10Z (req_0a1b2c3d) and 2025-11-04T14:08:22Z (req_0a1b2c3e). Their curl (sanitized):
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
     -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
     -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-mini-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}' \
     https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
They say adding --no-buffer didn't change it. They run behind Cloudflare Spectrum/proxy.

james-sre: If --no-buffer didn't help, likely client/proxy buffering or a middlebox coalescing small chunks. Ask them to run curl with explicit HTTP/1.1 and --no-buffer, and capture a packet trace:
```
curl -v --http1.1 -N --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -d '{...}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat
```
Also request tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i any -s 0 -w sse_issue.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443` (60s). I'll pull edge logs for those req ids. @bot-deploy can you surface the edge/worker traces for req_0a1b2c3d/e? :eyes: 

bot-deploy: Edge logs linked: https://internal-logs.redwood.ai/edge/1976/req_0a1b2c3d.log and https://internal-logs.redwood.ai/edge/1976/req_0a1b2c3e.log (scrubbed). Worker traces show backend delivered chunked responses with flushes at t=0s and t=26s. Attaching sample headers: `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, server: redwood-runtime/2.4.

eden-devex: Can we give the customer a minimal repro and a tiny helper to print chunk arrival times? Suggest this curl + small Python to show if chunks are buffered by OS or app: 
```
# curl to reproduce
curl -s --http1.1 -N --no-buffer -H "Accept: text/event-stream" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" 
  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-mini-v1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"stream test"}]}' 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat | 
# python one-liner prints time per line
python -c "import sys,time
for l in sys.stdin:
  print(time.time(), l[:120].rstrip())"
```
This will show gaps between lines. Also ask them to try bypassing Cloudflare (if possible) to rule out edge proxy.

maya-support: When you ask for the debug bundle, request the following:
1) PCAP (tcpdump -w) covering the session
2) curl output with `-v --http1.1 --no-buffer` (paste both stdout and verbose stderr)
3) Browser user-agent / node version if they used SDK
4) Any intermediate proxy/cloudflare config (Spectrum, WAF)
Also request `ngrep -W byline 'HTTP/1.1' port 443` if they can run it, or `ngrep -d any -W byline '' 'port 443'` for 30–60s. If they can't capture full PCAP, get the edge request IDs and timestamps.

frank-oncall: Customer answered: they ran tcpdump and attached sse_issue.pcap. They also ran curl --http1.1 --no-buffer and the gap persisted. Their proxy team confirmed Spectrum is enabled with TCP optimizations. They shared a short proxy trace showing keepalive resets and a 25s idle followed by a FIN/PSH ack.

james-sre: That fits proxy coalescing behavior — some front proxies delay small writes then flush on push or window thresholds. On our side we do frequent flushes but if the TLS record is coalesced by the proxy you'll see the client gap. Next steps:
- Reproduce internally by spinning up a small client with a proxy that mimics Spectrum's TCP optimizations (Nagle + delayed ACK + TLS coalescing).
- Try forcing larger initial chunk or explicit flush headers to see if that prevents coalescing (e.g., send initial dummy event of ~1KB).
- If repro, escalate to infra to add a small periodic keepalive flush for SSE responses in the runtime.

eden-devex: Also ask customer to try an experiment: change Content-Type to `text/plain` temporarily (if acceptable) to see whether any intermediate layer treats event-stream specially. And request their upstream TCP settings: `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_low_latency` etc.

maya-support: I'll collect the bundle: edge logs (linked), worker traces (attached), pcap from customer, curl outputs, and the proxy trace. Assigning follow-up to @james-sre for triage and to reach out to infra if we can repro in our env. I'll update the customer with suggested experiments and keep them in the loop. :thumbsup:
